title: Step 1: Count the Levels
story: The team's app.log keeps growing. Build a report script one step at a time.
goal: Print how many lines of each level (INFO, WARN, ERROR) app.log has, like INFO 2, in that order.
starter: # for each level, count matching lines

files.app.log:
2026-12-01 ERROR x one
2026-12-01 ERROR x one
2026-12-02 INFO ok fine

hints: grep -c counts matching lines. Put spaces around the level so you match the whole word.

for lvl in INFO WARN ERROR; do
  echo "$lvl $(grep -c " $lvl " app.log)"
done
socratic: Why grep -c instead of grep | wc -l?
What if a level never appears?
explain: In one sentence: what did you learn from “Step 1: Count the Levels”?
solution:
for lvl in INFO WARN ERROR; do
  echo "$lvl $(grep -c " $lvl " app.log)"
done

files.app.log:
2026-11-01 INFO web started
2026-11-01 ERROR db timeout
2026-11-01 WARN disk 91%
2026-11-02 ERROR db timeout
2026-11-02 INFO web started
2026-11-02 ERROR auth failed

alt:
for l in INFO WARN ERROR; do
  n=$(grep -c " $l " app.log)
  echo "$l $n"
done
